content: 1. A systematic review and meta-analysis on point-of-care infant diagnosis for HIV is currently under review and was published in The Lancet in 2022. 2. Otto AO, Rivera CG, Zeuli JD, and Temesgen Z conducted a review and evaluation of the hepatotoxicity of contemporary antiretroviral drugs, based on published clinical data. This study was published in Cells in 2021 (Volume 10, Article 1263). 3. The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) conducted a sub-study of HPTN 083 to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and acceptability of long-acting cabotegravir (CAB-LA) for HIV prevention among adolescent males. This study, identified as NCT04692077, was conducted between February 2020 and May 2023. 4. Similarly, NIAID conducted a sub-study of HPTN 084 to assess the safety, tolerability, and acceptability of CAB-LA for HIV prevention among adolescent females. This study, identified as NCT04824131, was conducted between November 2020 and May 2024. 5. The WHO Department of Global HIV, Hepatitis, and STI Programmes developed guidelines following WHO standards for guideline development (2nd edition, 2014). The process was overseen by the WHO Guideline Review Committee. 6. The WHO Secretariat coordinated the guideline development process, informed by the WHO Guideline Steering Group, which included representatives from various departments and regions. 7. To inform the guidelines, WHO conducted a systematic review of the safety, efficacy, and effectiveness of CAB-LA as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of HIV acquisition. This review was led by Dr. Virginia Fonner (Medical University of South Carolina/FHI 360) and Dr. Lara Lorenzetti, who also led the review on values and preferences regarding injectable PrEP, including CAB-LA. 8. The WHO Secretariat and guideline methodologist, Dr. George Rutherford, oversaw the collection, review, and grading of evidence. 9. Preliminary results from mathematical modeling studies on the population-level impact of CAB-LA introduction were presented by the HIV Prevention Trials Network (HPTN) Modeling Centre and the HIV Modeling Consortium. 10. Mary Henderson, an independent consultant, conducted a global survey and in-depth interviews with PrEP providers to gather their perspectives and preferences regarding CAB-LA for HIV prevention. 11. Amrit Ahluwalia from Tufts University presented findings on dolutegravir cross-resistance in individuals diagnosed with HIV after exposure to CAB-LA PrEP. 12. The GRADE method was used to rate the quality of evidence and determine the strength of recommendations. This approach defines the quality of evidence as the confidence in the reported estimates of effect being close to the actual effects. 13. The strength of a recommendation reflects the degree of confidence that the desirable effects (e.g., reduced morbidity and mortality, cost savings) outweigh the undesirable effects (e.g., drug resistance, toxicity). 14. Systematic reviews followed the PRISMA guidelines for reporting systematic reviews and meta-analyses. 15. A list of potential outcomes of interest was circulated among a subgroup of the Guideline Development Group (GDG) and discussed in virtual meetings. Critical outcomes were prioritized to focus evidence gathering and inform recommendations. 16. The GDG met virtually on March 9–10, 2022, to review supporting evidence and decision-making tables. Recommendations were made through consensus, facilitated by the methodologist. Voting was not required, but a two-thirds majority was agreed upon for decision-making if needed. 17. Draft guidelines were circulated for peer review among GDG members and the External Review Group. Comments were reviewed and incorporated into the final document, with consideration of any conflicts of interest. 18. All external contributors, including GDG and External Review Group members, completed WHO declarations of interest forms. A brief biography of each GDG member was published on the WHO HIV website for 14 days before the first meeting, with no public comments or objections received. 19. WHO conducted a web-based search to identify potential competing interests among GDG members. One member was removed due to conflicts of interest and did not participate in the GDG meeting. 20. A management plan for each declared conflict was agreed upon and recorded before the meeting. GDG members were also asked to declare any new or undeclared conflicts of interest at the start of the meeting. 21. All declaration of interest forms are maintained electronically at the WHO Department of Global HIV, Hepatitis, and STI Programmes for 10 years. 22. The External Review Group’s declarations of interest were reviewed by technical officers, and any identified conflicts were considered when interpreting comments during the external review process. 23. The WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2nd edition) was referenced during the process, and modeling studies on the introduction of CAB-LA in sub-Saharan Africa were conducted by the HIV Modeling Consortium Working Group. 24. Ahluwalia et al. characterized dolutegravir drug resistance in individuals diagnosed with HIV after exposure to CAB-LA PrEP, with findings published in AIDS (2022; Volume 36, Issue 13: Pages 1897–1898).
